column1: # TICK_SEAL_INVARIANTS.tsv
# The sealed ticks inside Ostler.app/Contents/Resources/ingest/<source>/tick.sh
# are the copies that EXECUTE. The daemon's run-source subcommand forks them so
# TCC responsibility stays on the signed parent. The vendored copies under
# vendor/<pkg>/bin/<feed>-bundle-tick.sh are the documented source of truth and
# are installed to ~/.ostler/bin/ but invoked by nothing.
# The sealed header asserts it is "a VERBATIM copy of the vendored tick ... Do
# not diverge." Nothing checked, and it diverged twice:
#   2026-08-14, measured on the live v1.0.26 box:
#     FDA preflight tokens   sealed 0   vendored 16   (control token 13 / 17)
#     the seal also kept the unbounded slot hold after the vendored side was
#     reasoned about and fixed.
# A BYTE DIFF IS THE WRONG INSTRUMENT. The two files legitimately differ:
# sealed 222 lines, vendored 268, different headers, no SOURCE_DIR placeholder
# in the seal. A diff would be red on every cut and would be switched off.
# So the invariant is not equality, it is SURVIVAL: every behavioural guarantee
# named below must be present on BOTH sides. Add a row whenever a tick gains a
# guarantee a customer depends on.
# Columns, tab-separated:
#   feed        one of: email imessage whatsapp spoken   (or * for all)
#   id          short stable name, appears in failure output
#   pattern     python regex, searched against the file text
#   why         one line: what breaks for the customer if it is absent
feed

column4: without it the feed never enrols as a waiter, so no holder is ever bounded on its behalf and it can starve forever
without it the payload runs outside the max-hold watchdog, so this feed's own hold is unbounded

the escape hatch must be testable; see the ordering check, which is enforced in code not here
